title: Vulnerability Characterization of Learning-Based Controllers in Networked Cyber-Physical Systems
summary: Studies how adversarial information patterns can deceive learning-based controllers in cyber-physical systems such as smart grids, robotic swarms, and autonomous vehicles, steering them toward biased or unsafe actions. The goal is secure-by-design solutions for safety-critical CPS.
objectives: A real-time reward manipulation scheme for learning-based controllers
Multi-level attacks on reward signals in distributed control using multiplayer Nash games
Data-enabled detection strategies

title: Spatio-temporal Modeling of Lithium-ion Battery Packs
summary: Cell-level battery models miss the strongly interconnected electro-thermal-aging behavior of real packs. This project develops a high-fidelity pack model at cell and module granularity and embeds continual learning in the battery management system for health-aware decisions that prevent failures and thermal runaway.
objectives: A strongly interconnected electro-thermal-aging pack model at cell/module granularity
A deep neural network learning scheme that captures spatial and temporal pack dynamics
Continual learning inside the BMS for health-conscious decision-making

title: NSF REU Site: Smart Personal Protective Equipment (SmaPP)
collaborators: Division of Engineering Technology, Oklahoma State University
summary: Nine undergraduates per summer (five at OSU, four at UAH ECE) gain multidisciplinary research experience on Smart Personal Protective Equipment: smart materials, heat flux measurement, wireless sensing of vital signs and radiation, and human perception of SmaPP.
objectives: Provide multidisciplinary research experience to undergraduates
Build a research mindset and prepare students for graduate study
Broaden participation of women and underrepresented groups
highlights: Auxetic material strength and impact testing
Heat flux measurement on SmaPP surfaces
Study of protective mask use on campus during COVID-19

title: Towards Autonomy in Uncertain Environments: Exploring Vistas Beyond Consensus
sponsor: Naval Surface Warfare Center, Panama City Division (DoD)
collaborators: Vignesh Narayanan, University of South Carolina
summary: Networked autonomous heterogeneous agents (NAHA) in uncertain naval environments must operate beyond consensus-based control, coping with limited communication, data privacy, and the need to isolate compromised agents.
objectives: Aperiodic communication protocols for distributed agents
Privacy-preserving, scalable learning for inference and filtering
Resource-conscious control robust to communication loss that can isolate compromised agents

title: AI-Enabled Autonomy of Robotic Inspection Platforms for Sustainability of Energy Infrastructure
summary: Robotic visual inspection of pipes, tanks, and hard-to-reach parts in energy, hydrogen, and carbon-capture infrastructure is still human-operated, slow, and error-prone. This project builds an AI-driven inspection platform with autonomous navigation and real-time defect identification.
objectives: Autonomous dynamic path planning and safe navigation
Closed-loop data collection
Real-time defect identification using deep learning on multimodal data

title: Resource-aware Intelligent Control of Cyber-Physical Systems
summary: Real-time CPS suffer from asynchronous feedback, network delays, packet dropouts, bandwidth limits, and computational cost, all of which degrade learning accuracy and control performance.
objectives: Self-learning distributed control that is computationally efficient
Inherently secure schemes that perform well under network constraints

title: Meta and Multimodal Learning for Smart Visual Borescope Inspection
sponsor: Oklahoma Center for the Advancement of Science and Technology (OCAST) and Baker Hughes
summary: AI-driven detection of cracks, spots, and corrosion for video borescopes that inspect narrow cavities. Deep learning needs large labeled datasets, which are scarce in this setting.
objectives: Algorithms that learn from both labeled and unlabeled data
Meta-learning and graph neural network architectures for few-shot defect detection

title: Intelligent Incipient Fault Detection System for Electric Vehicle Battery
sponsor: Transportation Consortium of South-Central States (TranSET), US DOT
summary: Detects internal faults in Li-ion batteries such as short circuits, lithium plating, and thermal rise in their early stages, using only measurable voltage, current, and surface temperature.
objectives: An incipient internal-fault detection scheme with root-cause analysis
A computationally efficient neural network suitable for embedded hardware

title: Smart Battery Management System for Electric Vehicles
sponsor: Transportation Consortium of South-Central States (TranSET), US DOT
summary: Studies normal and accelerated degradation to build SOC- and SOH-dependent parameter-varying circuit models, with real-time learning algorithms for embedded hardware.
objectives: Accurate SOC and SOH estimation
Support for charging optimization and power/energy management

title: Model-based Fault Detection System for Induction Motors
summary: A parameter estimation algorithm for an induction motor model, used to detect internal motor faults. Validated on a hydraulic testbed with NI CompactRIO data acquisition of three-phase voltages, currents, and speed, with code running on the cRIO's onboard FPGA.
objectives: Online parameter estimation of the induction motor model
Experimental validation of fault detection on a hydraulic testbed

title: Development of Wireless Heat Flux Sensor
sponsor: Technology and Business Development Office, Oklahoma State University
summary: An IoT wireless sensor that measures heat flux in fire conditions so firefighters can assess ignition risk and allocate resources, removing the need for water-cooled sensors with their tubing and wiring.
objectives: Transmit over cellular networks with low power and low data usage
Compute heat flux from raw temperature data from at least four sensors
